title: BBC ending Ski Sunday after nearly 50 years on air
dek: The BBC is discontinuing Ski Sunday after nearly 50 years, with the program's final broadcast scheduled before the 2027 season. The decision follows BBC budget cuts and shifting audience viewing habits toward digital platforms. Ed Leigh and Chemmy Alcott are the program's current presenting team, with Alcott having joined as lead co-presenter in 2021.
author: The GoCheckMySports Desk
key_fact: Ski Sunday, which first broadcast in 1978, is being axed as the BBC pivots winter sports coverage to digital platforms and the Winter Olympics.
bottom_line: The BBC's commitment to winter sports coverage at the Winter Olympics and on digital platforms will be the measure of whether Ski Sunday's discontinuation represents strategic consolidation or a genuine reduction in the corporation's winter sports portfolio. The 2027 winter sports season will show what replaces the program.
body: The BBC is ending Ski Sunday after nearly 50 years, according to BBC Sport. The program first broadcast in 1978. Ed Leigh and Chemmy Alcott are the program's most recent presenting team, with Alcott having become lead co-presenter alongside Leigh in 2021.

A BBC Sport statement explained: "Changing audience behaviours and the tough financial decisions needed to meet savings requirements mean BBC Sport must continually review how it delivers value for licence fee payers and serves audiences across all platforms. This decision forms part of that process."

Philip Bernie, head of BBC Sport events, said Ski Sunday "has been a truly iconic programme." He added: "Generations of viewers have enjoyed its coverage of the best in winter sports. We are enormously proud of the role it has played in bringing these moments to audiences across the UK, and extremely grateful to the brilliant people who have delivered them, not least the current outstanding team."

Bernie stated: "These decisions are never easy, but as audience viewing habits evolve and we work to deliver value for licence fee payers, we have to make tough choices. We remain committed to bringing audiences the very best of winter sport, above all at the Winter Olympics, across BBC Sport's platforms."
The Guardian's reporting notes the decision comes amid scrutiny over the BBC's approach to sports rights.
